summary: the shear relaxation modulus and the Green-Kubo shear viscosity from the autocorrelation of an off-diagonal stress at equilibrium

inputs.name: correlation
inputs.meaning: pairs [lag time, C] from lag time zero at a fixed spacing, C the autocorrelation of one off-diagonal stress component (or the mean over xy, xz, yz), in pressure squared of the run's units

inputs.name: volume
inputs.meaning: the volume of the system whose stress was sampled

inputs.name: thermal_energy
inputs.meaning: the thermal energy of the run

inputs.name: end
inputs.meaning: the lag time up to which the viscosity is integrated, one of the correlation's lag times, in its unit of time

outputs.name: modulus
outputs.meaning: pairs [lag time, G], G = V C / kT, the shear relaxation modulus in pressure of the run's units

outputs.name: viscosity
outputs.meaning: V/kT times the trapezoidal integral of C from zero to end: the shear viscosity when end lies where the integral has levelled off

outputs.name: samples_integrated
outputs.meaning: how many lag times the integral took, zero and end included

outputs.name: why
outputs.meaning: why nothing was computed; absent when computed

validity: linear response at equilibrium: the stress handed must be the system's whole off-diagonal stress, sampled densely enough for the trapezoidal rule; a kinetic part drawn afresh each step (as in Brownian dynamics) adds an uncorrelated spike at lag zero that the trapezoidal rule weighs by half a spacing, a bias the caller can see in the modulus

source.citation: Kim, Han, Kim, Li, Karniadakis and Lee (2018), Nature of intrinsic uncertainties in equilibrium molecular dynamics estimation of shear viscosity for simple and complex fluids, arXiv:1807.08063v1 (read 2026-11-21, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.08063v1; mat-20261121-kim-2018-green-kubo-uncertainty)
source.locus: equation (1): eta(t) = V/(kB T) times the integral from 0 to t of <pxy(0) pxy(t')>; equation (24): eta = V/(kB T) times the integral from 0 to infinity of C(t); section III: the integral was computed by the trapezoidal rule. Morozov and Spagnolie (2015), Introduction to Complex Fluids, chapter 1 of Complex Fluids in Biological Systems (read 2026-11-21, https://people.math.wisc.edu/~spagnolie/Papers/Introduction_to_Complex_Fluids.pdf; mat-20261121-morozov-spagnolie-2015-complex-fluids), equation (1.51): the Maxwell stress as the integral of the memory G exp(-(t - t')/lambda) over the past strain rate, so that V C(t)/kT is the relaxation modulus whose integral is the viscosity

note: Written for meta_agent/tasks/034 (the HOOMD-blue agent of an Oldroyd-B fluid of Hookean dumbbells, whose person chose 'Stress autocorrelation (Recommended)'). No value of the sources stands behind the worked cases: each is worked by hand in its worked field, on two unrelated kinds of system. v2 (tasks/034, failure bd-2): a value that is not a finite number is refused with a why, where v1 carried it into its output; seen when HOOMD-blue's pressure tensor, read on steps it had not computed, came back as not-a-number and v1 of exponential_decay_fit said fitted.
